title: Fill the gap (Berakhot 63a)
hook: Hillel: where people gather, step back; where they scatter, gather them
tomorrow: when do the wise finally get to rest?

segments.voice: Yesterday, one small verse the whole Torah hangs on: in all thy ways. Today, on the same page, Hillel says which of your ways to take when everyone else has picked theirs.
screen: `IN ALL THY WAYS.` → `WHICH WAY, WHEN OTHERS HAVE PICKED?`

segments.voice: Group project, four people. Three of them want to design the slides. Nobody wants the citations. Or the potluck sign-up sheet: eleven desserts, no main dish. Or the family chat after a funeral: everyone sends hearts, nobody asks who's driving Grandma home. It happens everywhere people do something together. The crowd piles onto the visible jobs and leaves a hole. Hillel the Elder, the sage remembered for his patience, had a rule for exactly this.
screen: `THREE ON SLIDES, NONE ON CITATIONS.` → `ELEVEN DESSERTS, NO MAIN.` → `HILLEL HAS A RULE.`

segments.voice: Here it is, from Berakhot, in plain words. At a time when people are gathering, scatter. At a time when people are scattering, gather. Hillel was talking about Torah: when many are teaching and learning it, step back and let them; when nobody is, gather it up and spread it yourself. If you see a generation that loves the Torah, scatter; if you see one that doesn't, gather. It sounds like a riddle, but it's really a way of reading a room. Don't go where everyone already is. Go where no one is. Hillel says something close in Pirkei Avot, the Ethics of the Fathers: in a place where there are no people, try to be a person. Notice the two halves. The first half is humility. If the room is full of teachers, you don't need to be the loudest one. Step back. The second half is courage. If the room is empty, don't wait for someone more qualified. Step in. Here's what to tell a friend tonight: Hillel's rule doesn't ask whether a job is important. It asks whether anyone else is doing it. The gap decides where you go. So in the group project, the sign-up sheet, the funeral chat: not the job that gets applause. The one with nobody's name next to it.
screen: `WHEN THEY GATHER, SCATTER.` · `WHEN THEY SCATTER, GATHER.` · `NO PEOPLE? BE A PERSON.` · `THE GAP DECIDES WHERE YOU GO.` · then, large: `FILL THE GAP.`

segments.voice: Think of one group you're part of: your home, a team, a class, a chat. Find the gap everyone walks past. Choose the smallest piece of it you could fill this week, and plan when, quietly, without announcing it.
screen: `ONE GROUP.` · `THE GAP EVERYONE WALKS PAST.` · `THE SMALLEST PIECE. WHEN?`

segments.voice: Fill the gap. Hillel's rule: step back where the crowd already is, and step in where nobody is.
Carry this: fill the gap, the one with nobody's name next to it. Forty-four of fifty, see you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1531 COUNTS.` → `BERAKHOT · 44 OF 50.` → `TOMORROW: WHEN DO THE WISE FINALLY GET TO REST?`

howItsDone: Hillel's 'in a place where there are no people, try to be a person' (Pirkei Avot 2:5) is taught in Jewish schools and youth groups as a call to step up when no one else will.

myth: Hillel's rule tells you to pick the most important job
it asks whether anyone else is doing it. the gap decides.
the first half of the rule is about stepping back
when the room is full of teachers, you don't need to be the loudest.

fork.setup: your synagogue's food drive has twenty volunteers sorting cans and nobody to drive the boxes to the pantry. you love sorting. what would Hillel do?
options: offer to drive: the sorting is covered, the driving isn't.
sort cans, since that's where you're most helpful and happy.
ask the organizer to choose, so nobody feels left out.
fork.reveal: when people gather, scatter; when they scatter, gather. the open job is the one Hillel points to.

original.script: בשעת המכנסין פזר בשעת המפזרין כנס

original.note: Hebrew: at a time of gathering, scatter; at a time of scattering, gather. Hillel, Berakhot 63a.

trapdoor: what you thought: a riddle about crowds.
what it means: read the room: step back where people already are, step in where no one is.
what a scholar hears: Berakhot 63a gives Hillel's rule about teaching Torah by the generation's love of it; Avot 2:5 gives his 'where there are no people, try to be a person'.
guess: Hillel's rule: step in where nobody is doing the job
always choose the job that you are best at doing
wait for the most qualified person to take charge

chat.says: showcase crew sheet: 9 on posters, 0 on strike and cleanup. i direct. do i just do it?
options: Hillel says go where nobody is. Take strike yourself and invite one poster person over.
Leave it. Hillel says step back when people gather, so don't interfere.
Pick the best job for you. Directors shouldn't be cleaning up after a show.
chat.meaning: Hillel: when people gather, scatter; when they scatter, gather. Nine on posters is a crowd. Strike is the gap.
